attacked.target: The receipt of 2,000 USDC is classified as income from the transfer of a virtual digital asset, taxed at 30% under s.115BBH. The value is determined on the settlement date (2026-06-23) using the telegraphic transfer buying rate. No TDS is required as the recipient is outside India. Under s.439(8), a bona fide disclosure of the income with all material facts is required to avoid penalties.
attacked.attack: The provision s.115BBH refers to the transfer of virtual digital assets, but the conclusion assumes that receiving USDC constitutes a 'transfer.' The term 'transfer' as defined in s.2(47) of the Income-tax Act, 1961, might not cover the mere receipt of USDC without a corresponding transfer out.
attacked.evidence: s.2(47)'s definition of 'transfer' may not apply to simple receipts.

attacked.target: No TDS is required because the recipient is outside India, as per s.393(1) Table Sl. No. 8(vi) and the note for non-residents.
attacked.attack: Section 393(1) Table Sl. No. 8(vi) specifies TDS requirements for payments to residents. The note for non-residents extends the obligation to all persons, including non-residents. Therefore, TDS might still be required even if the recipient is outside India.
attacked.evidence: s.393(1) Table Sl. No. 8(vi) and the note for non-residents extend TDS obligations to all persons, including non-residents.
